title: ED Triage Nursing Note
author: C. Huang, RN
summary: Arrived 0205 with mother: 5 weeks of thirst, peeing a lot and weight loss; vomiting since Sunday; deep fast breathing, fruity breath, drowsy. POC glucose HI. ESI 2, to resuscitation bay.
body:
**Arrival 0205** by private car with her mother (Danielle Thompson). Walked in with help.

**Story (mother and Maya)**
- About 5 weeks of being very thirsty (2-3 large sports drinks plus water every day), peeing "all the time", up 3-4 times a night; wet the bed once last week.
- Lost weight: 54.2 kg at her sports physical in August. Tired, falling asleep in class.
- Saturday: belly ache and nausea. Sunday from about 0900: vomited 6 times, could not keep fluids down. Sunday evening: breathing deep and fast, "really sleepy". Mother brought her in when she could not stay awake to talk.
- No fever, no diarrhea, no cough, no urinary burning. No known diabetes. No medicines. No allergies.

**Triage 0210**
T 99.1 F, HR 134, BP 108/64, RR 32 deep and regular (Kussmaul), SpO2 99% room air, pain 6/10 upper belly. Weight 48.6 kg (standing, with help). GCS 14 (E3 V5 M6). Fruity (acetone) breath. Dry cracked lips, no tears, capillary refill 3-4 seconds, hands cool.

**POC glucose 0225: HI (over 600).**

ESI 2. To resuscitation bay 2; Dr. Adeyemi at the bedside 0218. Two IVs and labs ordered (DKA order set).

title: ED Nursing Note - DKA Treatment and Response
author: C. Huang, RN
summary: Severe DKA treated per pediatric protocol: one 10 mL/kg bolus, insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h from 0400 (no bolus), two-bag fluids (no potassium) from 0545 with a KCl 10 mEq rider (peripheral IV rule). Glucose falling 50-56 per hour; GCS 14 unchanged; no headache.
body:
**Lines**
- 0220: 20 g IV left antecubital (labs drawn first, including the diabetes antibody tubes before any insulin).
- 0225: 20 g IV right forearm (saline lock for labs and IV push).

**Treatment**
- 0235 ondansetron 4 mg IV.
- 0240-0310 normal saline 500 mL (10 mL/kg) bolus.
- 0300 ECG: sinus tach 128, peaked T waves (K 5.6).
- 0315 normal saline 150 mL/h (no potassium yet: K 5.6, not yet voided).
- 0330 voided 350 mL (urine sample sent).
- **0400 regular insulin infusion 4.9 units/h (0.1 unit/kg/h), no bolus**, own pump, tubing primed with 20 mL. Independent double check with M. Ortiz, RN.
- 0545 two-bag system started, no potassium in the bags (peripheral IVs): Bag A 75 mL/h while the **KCl 10 mEq/100 mL rider** ran (0545-0645, potassium 4.7 at 0430, voiding), then Bag A 125 mL/h; Bag B (D10) hung at 0 mL/h.
- 0610 voided 400 mL.

**Response**
- POC glucose: HI (0225), 574 (0330), 552 (0400), 497 (0500), 441 (0600): falling about 55 per hour on insulin.
- Vitals 0615: HR 120, BP 112/70, RR 28 (still deep), SpO2 99%, T 98.8 F.
- Neuro checks hourly from 0300: GCS 14 each time, pupils 4 mm equal and brisk, no headache. Emesis 150 mL at 0230 only.

**Family**
Mother at the bedside, crying on and off: "I thought she was just drinking a lot because of volleyball." Father (Kevin) is a long-haul truck driver, driving home from Ohio; mother has called him.

title: ED to PICU Handoff (SBAR)
author: C. Huang, RN
summary: SBAR to the PICU RN: 16-year-old with new-onset type 1 diabetes in severe DKA; insulin 4.9 units/h since 0400, two-bag 125 mL/h (D0), KCl 10 mEq rider given 0545-0645; glucose 441 at 0600; K 4.7; hourly neuro checks normal.
body:
**S:** Maya Thompson, 16, new-onset type 1 diabetes in severe DKA. Full Code. No allergies. Weight 48.6 kg.

**B:** 5 weeks of thirst, peeing and weight loss (lost 5.6 kg); vomiting since Sunday. ED labs 0220: glucose 612, pH 7.04, pCO2 16, bicarbonate 5, anion gap 28, beta-hydroxybutyrate 7.8, Na 131, K 5.6, BUN 28, creatinine 1.3. 0430: glucose 520, pH 7.07, bicarbonate 6, K 4.7, beta-hydroxybutyrate 7.1.

**A:** Drowsy, GCS 14, oriented to person and place; Kussmaul breathing 28; HR 120, BP 112/70. No headache. Normal saline bolus 500 mL (0240), insulin 4.9 units/h from 0400 (no bolus), two-bag fluids from 0545 (no potassium in the bags): now Bag A 125, Bag B 0. KCl 10 mEq/100 mL rider 0545-0645 (first potassium). Glucose 441 at 0600 (falling about 55/h). Voided 350 and 400 mL. Emesis once (0230).

**R:** Hourly glucose: expect to start Bag B soon (glucose under 300 = 50/50). Potassium by riders per the 4-hour labs (no more than 10 mEq per hour). Hourly neuro checks: highest cerebral edema risk in the next 4-12 hours. Next labs 0830. Mother at the bedside; father driving home. Two IVs: left AC (fluids + insulin), right forearm (saline lock for labs).
